newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures follow cash to end higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures follow cash to end higher.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures followed stronger physical prices in the Gulf Coast to end higher Friday, industry sources said.
Physical prices in the Gulf Coast were said to be up one-to-three cents on expectations the U.S. could bomb Iraq this weekend and some short covering, the sources said.

October Henry Hub ended up 5.1 cents to settle at $1.864 per million British thermal units after trade as high as $1.880 and as low as $1.835. November ended up 5.4 cents at $2.072. The Nov/Oct spread again widened to 23.7 cents.
Cash prices, in part boosted by storage demand and Middle East tensions, rose on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes to talk in the mid-$1.80s, sources said.
NYMEX said an estimated 29,335 Henry Hub contracts traded.
NYMEX's October Permian contract did not trade but settled steady at $1.53.
On the KCBT, October settled 4.5 cents higher at $1.670. The East/West spread narrowed to 19.4 cents (NYMEX premium).
